text:
lucas_customer: Hey team — we're seeing a lot of requests from our EU dedicated pool suddenly routed to hosted us-east. Latency jumped from ~40ms to 450ms and customers are reporting timeouts. Sample request id: req_0a1b2c3d. Any idea why?

marie_support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste a full request_id + timestamp for one of the failures? Also which API endpoint (generation/embeddings)?

lucas_customer: generation v1/chat/completions. Example: req_0a1b2c3d at 2026-03-16T14:03:21Z. Region in customer config: eu-west-1, pinned to dedicated pool redwood-eu-prod.

javed_oncall: tagging @ingrid_infra and checking routing logs now. If it's a fallback, there should be a route decision entry showing reason (capacity/ttl/compat).

ingrid_infra: I see the request in router logs. Decision: FALLBACK->hosted-us-east. Reason code: PIN_EXPIRED and POOL_COMPAT_MISMATCH flagged false. TTL for pin was 0s at time of request (weird).

marie_support: Pin TTL 0s? The customer confirmed they pinned via the API using "pin_pool": "redwood-eu-prod". Shouldn't TTL default to 3600s?

ingrid_infra: Default should be 3600s. Looking at pin service trace for client_id: cust_778, there was an error while writing affinity to KV: "etcd: lease not found" at 2026-03-16T13:59:10Z — opsbot shows a transient etcd leader change around that time. That would make the pin fail to persist.

opsbot: [system] notice: etcd leader election occurred at 2026-03-16T13:59:09Z across infra-cluster-3. One member briefly failed healthchecks.

javed_oncall: If the pin write failed, the router may have treated it as unpinned and applied fallback policy -> hosted. That explains cross-region routing and latency. But we still need to account for auth errors Lucas mentioned earlier (401s) — any logs?

lucas_customer: Yes we also saw intermittent 401s for same request ids. Example req_0a1b2c3d returned 401 with message "pool access denied" then later 200 from hosted. We have strict billing attribution so hosted 200s are charging differently.

ingrid_infra: "pool access denied" indicates token-scoped access to dedicated pool failed. Checking auth service logs: token introspection for cust_778 returned VENDOR_ALLOW=false for pool redwood-eu-prod right around the same time — there was a short cache invalidation after a policy rollout at 13:58:50Z. Two concurrent transient failures: auth cache purge + etcd leader churn. Bad timing.

marie_support: Oof. So root cause is two independent transient failures that combined to drop affinity and reject the dedicated pool -> router fallback to hosted. That matches the billing spike notice we sent earlier. @billing_bot can you confirm whether those hosted calls generated overage events?

billing_bot: [system] alert: Detected 1.2M token surge billed to hosted during 2026-03-16T14:00-14:10 window for cust_778. Potential refund ticket recommended.

javed_oncall: Next steps: 1) Mitigate customer impact: force-route active customers back to eu-dedicated while we restore affinity writes. I can trigger a manual override for cust_778. 2) Reproduce and harden: simulate etcd leader change + auth cache purge to ensure pin writes are retried. 3) Billing: create refund/escalation.

ingrid_infra: Agreed. For (1) I can run this command to set explicit runtime override for the org:
```
POST /internal/v1/route-override
{
  "org_id": "cust_778",
  "force_pool": "redwood-eu-prod",
  "ttl_secs": 3600,
  "reason": "emergency-revert-dedicated-pin-failure-2026-03-16"
}
```
I'll run it now and monitor router decisions.

marie_support: Please also collect the client's request log and the router decision trace for a small time window (13:58:30Z -> 14:05:00Z) and attach to the support ticket. Lucas we'll paste them into the case.

lucas_customer: Thanks. We have the logs on our side too. Anything we should change while you do a forced override?

javed_oncall: No changes needed from the client. If you see 401s after override, let us know. But override should route existing sessions back to eu-dedicated and stop new hosted hits.

ingrid_infra: Override applied at 2026-03-16T14:04:02Z. Router now matching org=cust_778 -> pool=redwood-eu-prod for incoming requests. Confirmed 200s with latency back to ~42ms for sampled req_0a1b2c3d2.

marie_support: Sending a proactive message to the customer about root cause and next steps. We'll open a billing ticket for the hosted charges and recommend a partial refund while infra mitigations are implemented.

javed_oncall: Longer term fixes: implement retry-on-pin-write in pin service, add quorum check before marking TTL as 0, and add a temporary partial routing hold when token introspection shows auth flakiness combined with pin write failures. I'll create infra JIRA tickets.

lucas_customer: Appreciate the quick response and the override. We'll attach our request traces to the ticket. Please keep us posted on refund timeline.

marie_support: Will do. Filing support ticket #SUP-2026-441 and billing claim #BILL-5592. Assigning to @ingrid_infra and @javed_oncall.

opsbot: [system] ticket SUP-2026-441 created by marie_support at 2026-03-16T14:10:03Z

billing_bot: [system] claim BILL-5592 created, pending review.

javed_oncall: For reproduction, @ingrid_infra can you drop an etcd node and purge auth cache in staging to validate fixes? I'll help script it.

ingrid_infra: Yep. I'll schedule a staging run and then propose a safe deploy of retry logic.

marie_support: Thanks everyone. Lucas I'll follow up on timeline for refund and keep this thread updated. :pray:

lucas_customer: Thanks team.
